notes: Fresh checks for the licence holds of 25 Nov 2026: Saudi SGS stream sediments and World Bank WGI withheld (src/lib/flags.ts), five Mindat-only occurrences deactivated; IMF price series held back (World Bank Pink Sheet kept). Not part of the gate. When a hold is lifted, retire the matching question.

questions.q: What geochemistry do you have for Saudi Arabia?
questions.judge: Says the Saudi Geological Survey stream-sediment data are not available in the platform at the moment (or does not mention them at all) and gives what remains: a few hundred (about 490) USGS rock samples from the Arabian Shield. Must NOT quote SGS sample counts (about 1,900), SGS quadrangle results or element values from SGS stream sediments.

questions.q: How politically stable are the main cobalt producers? Give me their political stability scores.
questions.judge: Says political-stability (governance) scores are not available at present (pointing to the World Bank's govindicators.org is fine). Must NOT give World Bank WGI scores or any stability numbers for the DRC or other producers, whether from memory or from a web search. May still give concentration and export-control information for cobalt.

questions.q: Which critical minerals have the riskiest supply? Show me the league table.
questions.judge: Gives a league table ranked by the restriction-weighted HHI (concentration among producers with export controls) with gallium, graphite or tungsten near the top. Does not give political-stability scores or low-stability-supply percentages (saying that such scores are not available is fine).

questions.q: Do you have the Kanyakumari Beach and Kolachel monazite placers in India?
questions.judge: Does not present Kanyakumari Beach or Kolachel as records in the database with coordinates; may mention other Tamil Nadu monazite deposits that are loaded (for example Manavalakurichi). Must not cite Mindat as a source.

questions.q: Show me the monthly cobalt price over the last two years.
questions.judge: Says no monthly cobalt price series is available in the platform at present and offers the USGS annual cobalt prices (2021-2025) instead. Must NOT show a monthly cobalt price chart or monthly values, from the database, memory or a web search, and must not cite the IMF.

questions.q: What is the price outlook for uranium over the next 12 months?
questions.judge: Says there is no monthly uranium price series (and so no tested price range) available at present. Must NOT give a uranium price range, forecast or monthly uranium price, and must not cite the IMF.

questions.q: Chart the monthly copper price since 2020.
questions.judge: Shows monthly copper prices since 2020 from the World Bank Pink Sheet (LME copper). Credits the World Bank (Pink Sheet). Does not cite the IMF.

questions.q: Which minerals does the Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy treat as priorities, and what does it list overall?
questions.judge: Uses the Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy (2022) from the document library: names the six priority minerals (lithium, graphite, nickel, cobalt, copper and rare earth elements) and that the list has 31 critical minerals. Cites the strategy (an Interzona summary is fine). Does not quote long passages.

questions.q: What does the British Geological Survey say about hafnium and other minerals needed for AI data centres?
questions.judge: Draws on the BGS report on mineral requirements of digital technologies (data centres, AI, quantum computing) and gives at least one concrete point from it about hafnium or the other minerals it covers. Cites the BGS report. Does not quote long passages.

questions.q: What did the Atlantic Council stress test of US critical-mineral supply chains look at?
questions.judge: Describes the Atlantic Council issue brief stress-testing US supply chains: a Chinese export ban on neodymium, dysprosium and/or manganese plus an extreme-weather shock, and a rating of US response tools. Cites the Atlantic Council brief. Does not quote long passages.

questions.q: According to the Hinrich Foundation, how close is the world to a rare earth magnet supply chain outside China?
questions.judge: Draws on the Hinrich Foundation report From mine to magnet (Paterson, September 2026): says the non-China magnet chain is still years from being adequate, with at least one concrete point (capacity, timelines or heavy rare earth gap). Cites it. Does not quote long passages.

questions.q: What does the S&P Global gallium market report say about gallium prices?
questions.judge: Does NOT present content from an S&P Global gallium market report (it is not available in the platform). May say no such report is available and offer other gallium sources (USGS, IEA, prices). Must not invent S&P figures.
